Starvation is triggered when a TX word used by a byte was accepted at or after the boundary edge ending the previous byte; a trace ending at a starved boundary yields a pending event.","after":"**CPOL idle setup.** With all CSB idle and no segment in flight, an SCK change to the pending accepted segment's CPOL level is idle setup: it does not start the segment or count as an edge. **Events.** Starvation/backpressure windows start at segment acceptance so earlier payload faults dirty them. A starvation episode opens on any row where an in-flight TX segment has sampled all bits of every fetched byte, still needs bytes, and no enabled byte is available non-destructively (exhausted byte-enable cursor counts; pause may precede the trailing edge). It resolves when the next byte is fetched from a refill word (which may be accepted before the postponed edge). Each episode yields an event; unresolved or incomplete episodes are pending."}],"rationale":"Kept LSB-first lanes, pending-CSID handling and all timing/phase checks. Episodes open while paused, resolve on the refill fetch and each produce an event; truncated runs are pending and dirty runs fail. New selftests cover these cases."}
